title: High-resolution Patterning Using Two Modes of Electrohydrodynamic Jet: Drop on Demand and Near-field Electrospinning
protocol: Fill the filtered silver nanoparticle (AgNP) ink in the ink reservoir of the EHD printing system.
Place a glass capillary [inner diameter (ID) of 1 mm] in the thermal puller.
Set the parameters of the thermal puller; for example, the heating temperature in the range of 580 - 590 °C and a pulling speed of around 18 mm/s.
Operate the thermal puller with the set parameters to apply heat at the center of the capillary and pull at both ends to make a nozzle with an ID of 5 µm.
Adjust the glass nozzle length by cutting the glass nozzle via a glass cutter.
Assemble the nozzle to the nozzle holder and the connector, which are connected to the ink reservoir via polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tubing.
Apply air pressure of 15 ~ 20 kPa to the ink reservoir using the air-pressure controller.
Monitor the ink flow through the transparent glass nozzle and tubing.
Ensure no air is trapped inside the tube and the nozzle when supplying the ink.
Keep applying air pressure until ink appears at the nozzle tip.
Reduce the pressure to around 12 kPa after ink appears at the nozzle tip.
Fix the assembled nozzle head in the printing system.
Place a glass substrate on the vacuum chuck of the substrate holder.
Turn on the vacuum pump to hold the substrate.
Adjust the Z-axis stage to set the stand-off distance to approximately 100 μm.
Use the side-view image from the monitoring camera to estimate the stand-off distance by measuring from the nozzle tip to its reflection.
Increase the DC voltage gradually until ink drips from the nozzle tip.
Reduce the DC voltage slightly until no further ink dripping occurs.
Set a negative pulse voltage with parameters trise = 0 ~ 100 µs, tdwell = 300 µs, and tfall = 0 µs in the software menu.
Apply the negative pulse voltage at the substrate holder.
Adjust the magnitude of the pulse voltage to produce one droplet per single pulse.
Adjust the DC background and pulse voltages to obtain the target droplet size on the substrate.
Observe the jetted dots on the substrate using the side view camera image.
Load a bitmap image in the printing tab of the printing software.
Convert the loaded bitmap image into a binary image.
Set the parameters for binary image printing.
Set the drop interval at 10 µm.
Start printing using the selected bitmap on the target location in the substrate.
Load the CAD information for printing.
Set the parameters for vector printing.
Set the drop interval at 3 µm.
Set the jetting frequency at 10 Hz.
Ensure an overlapping of about 30% for line patterns to avoid larger line widths.
Mix ethanol and deionized (DI) water with a volume ratio of 3:1 to prepare solvent 1.
Stir a mixture of 0.3 g poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO, Mwt = 400,000) and 9.7 g solvent 1 for more than 6 hours at room temperature using a magnetic stirrer.
Mix Ag nano paste ink with the prepared polymer solution in a weight ratio of 5:1 by using a vortex mixer for 10 minutes to obtain NFES ink.
Fill the prepared NFES ink in the syringe.
Connect the syringe with a nozzle via the connecting tube.
Install the syringe in the syringe motor attached to the printing system.
Place a substrate on the vacuum chuck and turn on the vacuum pump to hold the substrate during the printing.
Control the Z-position (stage) to adjust the stand-off distance.
Operate the syringe pump to fill the NFES ink in the nozzle assembly and generate an ink flow with an initial flow rate of 50 µL/min.
Set a target flow rate of 1 µL/min when the ink flows out of the nozzle tip.
Connect the DC voltage source to the nozzle connector and connect the ground voltage to the substrate holder.
Gradually increase the DC voltage to 1.5 kV.
Start the idle printing with a printing speed of 300 mm/s for more than 10 min to obtain a steady-state flow.
Adjust the printing parameters such as the DC voltage and flow rate during the idle printing to obtain the desired printing results.
Print the selected pattern on the substrate using pre-determined printing parameters.
